title: 2003 IMO Problem 4
statement:
Let \(ABCD\) be a cyclic quadrilateral.
Let \(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\) be the feet of perpendiculars
from \(D\) to lines \(\overline{BC}\), \(\overline{CA}\) and \(\overline{AB}\), respectively.
Show that \(PQ = QR\) if and only if the
bisectors of angles \(ABC\) and \(ADC\) meet on segment \(\overline{AC}\).

solutions.text:
Let \(\gamma\) denote the circumcircle of \(ABCD\).
The condition on bisectors is equivalent to \((AC;BD)_\gamma = -1\).
Meanwhile if \(\infty\) denotes the point at infinity along Simson line \(\overline{PQR}\)
then \(PQ = QR\) if and only if \((PR;Q\infty) = -1\).

Let rays \(BQ\) and \(DQ\) meet the circumcircle again at \(F\) and \(E\).

[Diagram omitted from this imported TeX transcription.]

Lemma.
 [EGMO Proposition 4.1]
 Then \(\overline{BE} \parallel \overline{PQR}\).

Proof.
 Since \(\measuredangle DQR = \measuredangle DAR = \measuredangle DAB = \measuredangle DEB\).

Now we have
\[ (PR;Q\infty) \overset{B}{=} (CA;FE)_\gamma
 \overset{Q}{=} (AC;BD)_\gamma \]
as desired.
